subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add a public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence contract for cron `every` schedules and heartbeat cadence, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval while relying on heartbeat phase and cron-expression stagger for anti-herd behavior?
rationale: The remaining source gap is clear, but the fix changes public scheduling semantics and persisted config/protocol shape, and repository policy treats config/default/scheduler surfaces as compatibility-sensitive product decisions.

options.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit `every` scheduling contract with protocol/schema, CLI, persistence, docs, upgrade tests, and status/list visibility before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve `everyMs` plus `anchorMs` as the stable fixed-interval contract and limit anti-herd behavior to heartbeat phase spreading and cron-expression staggering.

options.title: Accept broader prime mode
options.body: Add prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls across heartbeat and cron, with a larger migration and observability plan.

recommendation.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit `every` scheduling contract with protocol/schema, CLI, persistence, docs, upgrade tests, and status/list visibility before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the current cron-expression stagger surface and is the strongest owner for deciding whether `every` should grow a new public scheduling contract.
